criteria.text: I can distinguish a runtime writer from initial-only seed data and resource descriptions in my world table.
I see two runtime writers rejected while repeated actors and hyphenated names keep their meaning.
I see one warning naming present seed branches with no declaration, without inheriting writers or inventing schemas.
I get the same counts, diagnostics and separate warnings in text and JSON without a service call or source change.

boundary: real native CLI argv/runContracts with Git-visible synthetic files; paired text/JSON; no Runtime entry or private fixture data

setup.case_files: Each case starts empty, applies delete_files then set_files; all authored files are Git-visible. A deleted absent file remains absent.
setup.observations: Exact projections on supplied diagnostic/warning fields, with no additional warnings or diagnostics. Messages are finite nonblank strings; missing-writer messages name every world_keys path and quantity with singular for one. Missing-schema messages use 1 world key for one and N world keys for plural. Text carries the same facts. text_facts are required substrings only, not complete wording pins. checked_records counts the two independently declared schemas whenever shapes.md is supplied, even if only one is selected. Preserve all source bytes/modes; all effect counters stay zero. Initial-only warnings are one per unique exact path; their finite nonblank messages name that path. Placeholder matching changes missing-row coverage only, never ownership or schema value checks.
